neighbours.label: concessive or affirming discourse adverb ('of course', 'at least', 'certainly'); the - pole is the restricting side ('merely', 'only', 'simply')
fire: The plan will be very difficult, at least until the funding arrives.
Much depends, though certainly not everything, on early training.
I cover, of course, the factors that changed the industry.
It goes without saying, of course, that nobody follows the rules.
The stamp is of course the most valuable one in the album.
The repair should take two weeks, or at least that is the estimate.
She was certainly the best player on the team that year.
We will need, of course, a full report before the meeting.
quiet: The plan will be very difficult until the funding arrives.
Much depends on early training and on good coaching.
I cover the factors that changed the industry in detail.
It turned out that nobody followed the rules that week.
The stamp is the most valuable one in the whole album.
The repair should take two weeks according to the estimate.
She was the best player on the team that year.
We will need a full report before the meeting starts.
